accepted.s: Humayun ascended the Mughal throne on which date?
accepted.x: Humayun took the throne on 29 December 1530, three days after Babur's death.
accepted.tq: Use precise date recall where close chronological distractors are given.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT mentioned as one of Humayun's initial problems?
o: Rivalry of Kamran, Askari and Hindal
The challenge from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat-Malwa
accepted.x: Humayun's initial problems included his rival brothers, the Afghans, Bahadur Shah of Gujarat-Malwa and an empty treasury. Rana Sanga was not listed among these problems.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the closely related group of contemporary challenges.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At Dourah, Humayun defeated the Afghans and drove which person from Jaunpur?
accepted.x: Humayun defeated the Afghans at Dourah and drove Mahmud Lodi from Jaunpur.
accepted.tq: Match the battlefield with the specific opponent or consequence.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gujarat, 1535 — Bahadur Shah allowed the Portuguese to fortify Diu
accepted.x: When pressed by Humayun in Gujarat in 1535, Bahadur Shah allowed the Portuguese to fortify Diu. Humayun was defeated at Chausa and Kannauj, while he defeated Sikandar Sur at Sirhind.
accepted.tq: Separate victories from defeats by checking the result attached to each event.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Humayun's defeat at Chausa in 1539 was inflicted by
accepted.x: Sher Khan defeated Humayun at Chausa in 1539.
accepted.tq: Identify the ruler associated with the decisive action at the named battlefield.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Kannauj and Bilgram:
1. They refer to the same battle fought in 1540.
2. The battle was won by Sher Khan.
3. Humayun was driven into exile after the battle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Kannauj and Bilgram are two names for the same 1540 battle. Sher Khan won it, and Humayun was consequently driven into exile.
accepted.tq: Test whether apparently different names denote the same historical event.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During his exile, Humayun married
accepted.x: Humayun married Hamida Banu Begum during his exile.
accepted.tq: Use a person–event association rather than a broad dynastic identification.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Akbar was born at Amarkot in 1542 during Humayun's
accepted.x: Akbar was born at Amarkot in 1542 while Humayun was in exile.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an event occurring during exile from events occurring before or after it.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who helped Humayun retake Kandahar and Kabul during his exile?
accepted.x: Safavid ruler Shah Tahmasp of Persia helped Humayun retake Kandahar and Kabul.
accepted.tq: Identify the foreign ally from a set of contemporary Indian rulers.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Humayun returned to India in July 1555 primarily by exploiting
o: the defeat of Babur at Chanderi
accepted.x: Humayun exploited quarrels among Sher Shah's successors and returned in July 1555.
accepted.tq: Link a political circumstance to the ruler's successful return.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence of Humayun's victories after his return in 1555?
accepted.x: After returning, Humayun defeated Sikandar Sur at Machhiwara and Sirhind, and then took Delhi and Agra.
accepted.tq: Follow the first and last events to eliminate reversed sequences.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Humayun died in January 1556 after falling from the stairs of
o: the Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri
the Sher Mandal library in Purana Qila
accepted.x: Humayun died in January 1556 after falling from the stairs of the Sher Mandal library in Purana Qila.
accepted.tq: Use the exact location to distinguish similar Mughal monuments and buildings.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Samugarh?
o: It was fought in 1539 between Babur and Mahmud Lodi.
It was fought in 1540 between Humayun and Sher Khan.
It was fought in 1555 between Humayun and Hemu.
It was fought in 1658 between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh.
accepted.x: The Battle of Samugarh was fought in 1658 between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh. It was not a battle of Humayun's return in 1555.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely placed Mughal dates and similarly named battles.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was Babur's last battle?
accepted.x: The Battle of Ghaghra in 1529 was Babur's last battle, fought against the Afghans of Bihar-Bengal led by Mahmud Lodi.
accepted.tq: Use the terminal event in a dated sequence to identify the answer.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Second Battle of Panipat was fought on 5 November 1556.
2. Akbar and Bairam Khan fought against Hemu.
3. The battle marked the end of Afghan power.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Second Battle of Panipat was fought on 5 November 1556, when Akbar and Bairam Khan defeated Hemu, ending Afghan power.
accepted.tq: Combine date, opposing sides and historical consequence in one statement set.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The result of the Battle of Haldighati in 1576 was that it was
o: a decisive victory of Maharana Pratap over Man Singh
a decisive Mughal victory ending all resistance
a defeat of Akbar by Sher Khan
accepted.x: The Battle of Haldighati in 1576, fought between Man Singh and Maharana Pratap, was not decisive.
accepted.tq: Watch for exaggerated outcome words such as decisive and all.
accepted.sec: Humayun - battles in order, exile, return, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Farid, who later became Sher Shah Suri, belonged to the
accepted.x: Sher Shah was born Farid and belonged to the Afghan Sur tribe.

accepted.x: Farid studied at Jaunpur and managed his father's jagir from 1511.
accepted.tq: Separate an early career date from later military and accession dates.

accepted.s: Who gave Farid the title 'Sher Khan'?
accepted.x: Bahar Khan of Bihar gave Farid the title Sher Khan after he slew a tiger.
accepted.tq: Link a title with the person who conferred it and the associated deed.

accepted.x: Sher Khan served Babur and later became deputy regent and the de facto ruler of Bihar.
accepted.tq: Track the correct region in a ruler's rise to power.

accepted.s: Which battle was a turning point in Sher Shah's rise?
accepted.x: Sher Shah's victory at Surajgarh was a turning point in his rise. He subsequently took Gaur in 1538.
accepted.tq: Identify the event specifically described as the turning point rather than a later conquest.

accepted.s: Sher Shah assumed the title 'Sher Shah' after the Battle of
accepted.x: After defeating Humayun at Chausa in 1539, Sher Khan assumed the title Sher Shah. He took the throne after Kannauj in 1540.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the event connected with assuming a title from the later accession event.

accepted.s: Which of the following places was NOT included among Sher Shah's listed conquests?
accepted.x: The listed conquests were Malwa, Raisen and Marwar. Kandahar was associated with Humayun's recovery with Safavid help.
accepted.tq: Find the geographically related but historically separate place.

accepted.s: Raisen was conquered by Sher Shah from
accepted.x: Sher Shah's conquest of Raisen was associated with Puran Mal.

accepted.s: Sher Shah's remark about nearly losing Hindustan 'for a handful of bajra' was made in connection with the battle of
accepted.x: The remark referred to the hard-fought Battle of Samel against Maldeo of Marwar.
accepted.tq: Use a memorable quotation as a clue to the associated battle and opponent.

accepted.s: Which pair is correctly matched regarding the Rajput resistance to Sher Shah?
o: Jaita and Kumpa — generals of Maldeo of Marwar
Jaita and Kumpa — generals of Bahadur Shah of Gujarat
Puran Mal and Maldeo — generals of Sher Shah
Maldeo and Sikandar Sur — generals of Hemu
accepted.x: Jaita and Kumpa were associated with Maldeo of Marwar and fought with great valour against Sher Shah at Samel.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure person–place association and eliminate swapped commanders.

accepted.s: Sher Shah died in 1545 in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of
accepted.x: Sher Shah died in 1545 in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of Kalinjar.

accepted.s: Islam Shah, also known as Jalal Khan, ruled during
accepted.x: Islam Shah, whose original name was Jalal Khan, ruled from 1545 to 1553.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a successor's regnal period from the reigns of Humayun and Sher Shah.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Muhammad Adil Shah is correct?
o: He ruled in the east and his general and minister was Hemu.
He ruled Delhi throughout Humayun's exile and appointed Bairam Khan.
He was the ruler of Marwar who resisted Sher Shah.
He helped Humayun recover Kandahar from the Safavids.
accepted.x: Muhammad Adil Shah ruled in the east, and Hemu served as his general and minister.
accepted.tq: Test the ruler–region–minister relationship while avoiding swapped roles.
accepted.sec: Sur successors - Islam Shah, Adil Shah, Hemu  [other exams]

accepted.s: Hemu seized Agra and Delhi in 1556 and assumed the title
accepted.x: After occupying Agra and Delhi in 1556, Hemu took the title Vikramaditya.
accepted.tq: Match a political achievement with the title assumed immediately thereafter.
accepted.sec: Sur successors - Islam Shah, Adil Shah, Hemu  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Hemu:
1. He was the Hindu minister-general of Adil Shah.
2. He occupied Agra and Delhi in 1556.
3. He was defeated at the Second Battle of Panipat after an arrow struck his eye.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Hemu served Adil Shah, occupied Agra and Delhi, and was captured after being struck in the eye at the Second Battle of Panipat.
accepted.tq: Combine office, territorial action and battlefield outcome in a single factual set.
accepted.sec: Sur successors - Islam Shah, Adil Shah, Hemu  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political situation after Sher Shah's death?
o: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat became the undisputed successor.
Islam Shah succeeded him, followed by rival claims involving Adil Shah and Sikandar Sur.
Humayun immediately succeeded him without opposition and ruled continuously.
Hemu succeeded him as Sultan and ended all Afghan rivalry.
accepted.x: Islam Shah succeeded Sher Shah. Later, Muhammad Adil Shah in the east and Sikandar Sur fought each other amid the fragmentation of Sur power.
accepted.tq: Infer the succession pattern from the sequence of rulers and competing claimants.
accepted.sec: Sur successors - Islam Shah, Adil Shah, Hemu  [other exams]
